name: tutorial-playthrough
description: Full tutorial playthrough at Tutorial Pit: hiring employees, seismic surveying, drill planning, blasting, contract management, building infrastructure, and completing the campaign introduction

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:6 start:15,15 diameter:0.089
steps.description: #553: the drag rectangle was shrunk from (15,15)-(25,25) to (15,15)-(21,21). Command and click stay equivalent -- the Drill panel's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3) computes cols/rows as round(size/spacing)+1, so round(6/3)+1 = 3x3 = 9 holes for this rectangle, exactly what the command declares. The shrink is the point: drill_hole is now real queued work, and a lone driller with one drill_rig and no living quarters collapses from fatigue partway through a pattern (sandbox-measured: hole 9 of 9 lands at tick 119, hole 16 of 16 not until tick ~400). 16 holes would have made this file a study of one worker's stamina rather than a tutorial playthrough. depth stays 6, the panel default this step never clicks away from. Blast consequences re-measured at the smaller pattern rather than carried over -- see the blast step below. diameter:0.089 added (issue #553 shared-mechanism finding, same as rock-fragmenter-breaking.json/hauling-gate.json/nav-*-visual.json/save-load-visual.json/weather-flood.json): the real grid-tool confirm always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), while an omitted diameter: on this console command fell back to a different console-only default (0.15, mining.ts) -- computeDrillHoleDurationTicks scales drill duration by diameter, so the omission kept the drill_rig busy (fuelCostPerTick) for extra ticks command mode never should have spent. Confirmed exact: adding the real default here reproduces interaction mode's own $126,884 figure at the very next charge step, and the same fixed $108 offset carries unchanged through every remaining cash checkpoint in this file (the second drill_plan below needs no change -- its own diameter default happens not to move the total further).

expect.note: #553: confirming the grid only orders the 9 holes -- they are ghosts until the driller drives the drill_rig to each one, so holeCount is 0 here and the wait is the step below.

Finding #40: the corrected 16-hole grid (vs. the originally-declared 9) is dense and energetic enough to kill both employees standing nearby -- confirmed via direct trace (state.damage.deathCount goes 0->2, both the surveyor and the driller, neither of whom this file ever dispatches away from the blast area first). This is a real, verified consequence of fixing the grid-spacing bug, not a scenario-authoring mistake to route around: the file's own later steps never depend on employee #1 or #2 specifically again (later roles are filled by newly-hired employees #3/#4), so the playthrough continues normally with a smaller, grimmer workforce -- exactly what a real player who dragged this same rectangle would experience.

#513/#581: the accept click is scoped to `[data-contract-id="12"]`, the contract this step's `command` names. Unscoped, `.bs-contract-accept` always resolves to whichever offered card is first in the DOM, so command mode accepted contract #12 literally while interaction mode accepted whatever led the list -- two channels driving different contracts while both reported pass, because nothing asserted here can tell them apart (`activeContractCount` counts accepts, not identities). `level1-win-efficient` is what that costs once a `[data-contract-id]`-scoped assertion is added on top: its guard failed with its control absent from the DOM entirely, red on `main`, cause pointing nowhere near the accept step. ContractsPanel sets `data-contract-id` on offered cards (`makeOfferedCard`), so scoping removes the DOM-order coupling rather than baking around it. #554: id renumbered from the file's original 5 -- `charge hole:*` is now queued, real-time work, so by this point in the run the tick clock is far past where it used to be, and the contract-offer pool (`REFRESH_INTERVAL`/`MAX_AVAILABLE`, Contract.ts) has cycled past id 5 entirely. #12 is the live id verified against `contract list` at this file's real tick count (251) -- a rubble_disposal contract, same type as the original.

BLOCKED, and deliberately not converted to a click: the ACTIVE card's DELIVER button is genuinely disabled at this point. ContractsPanel disables the amount box, MAX and DELIVER together whenever maxDeliverable = min(contract remaining, stored material) is 0, and a direct trace of this file shows 0.0 kg of rubble in storage against a 340 kg contract (#554 renumber: was contract #5/430kg -- see the accept step above for why the id moved). Still true post-#552 (self-dispatching hauling): no debris_hauler exists yet at this point in the file (bought only much later, step 28) -- there is nothing for auto-dispatch to claim with yet, manual or otherwise. The console command is no better: it returns success:false ("Not enough stored material: 0.0 kg available") and command mode only fails a step on a thrown exception, so `contract deliver 12 amount:5000` is a silent no-op in BOTH modes today. `expect.blocked` is what now pins it down -- the button must be in the DOM and refused, with `expect.usable` on the panel's own storage link proving the panel is really open, so "blocked" cannot pass just because nothing is on screen.

expect.note: stays active/undelivered -- economy-full-loop.json is the file that actually hauls stock and completes a delivery.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:6 diameter:0.089 start:24,24
steps.description: #553: pattern moved from (8,8)-(12,12) to (24,24)-(28,28). The freight_warehouse built at (6,6) earlier in this file occupies ground the old rectangle reached: two of its four holes were ordered onto cells no driller can stand on, so they stayed ghosts forever and the charge step below saw 2 holes instead of 4. Nothing was wrong pre-#553 because confirming a plan wrote all four holes out regardless of who could reach them. Original note follows -- spacing corrected from 4 to 3 (the Drill panel's real default, DEFAULT_SPACING_M): the click drags a 4-unit (8,8)-(12,12) rectangle, and round(4/3)+1 = 2 either way, so the hole COUNT this file originally declared (2x2=4) already happened to match by coincidence -- but the declared spacing value did not match what the click actually uses, so corrected for accuracy per the same principle as the first drill_plan step above, even though no assertion here was actually at risk. diameter:0.089 added (issue #586 CI, this PR): this command is what both command mode AND a bare-command replay through the browser actually run for this step (the click flow's own grid-tool confirm handler always sends its panel default DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089, same as the first drill_plan step, which already carries diameter:0.089 for exactly this reason) -- omitted here, the command fell back to the console-only default (0.15, mining.ts), a 68% bigger diameter that computeDrillHoleDurationTicks (DrillPlan.ts) scales hole-drilling duration by. Direct trace: with the console default, driller #5 spends enough extra active-drilling ticks over the pattern-2 wait to fatigue-collapse mid-pattern and get auto-routed to rest near living_quarters (17,13), safely outside the blast footprint when it fires. With the real diameter both a live UI click and this corrected command now share, #5 instead finishes all 4 holes with ticks to spare and is standing at (27,27) -- one of the pattern's own holes -- when the blast goes off, the same mechanism that already kills employee #2 in blast 1. That is the real, common-diameter outcome verified live (3 consecutive clean interaction-mode reruns, deathCount 0->2 unchanged from blast 1, matching the note on the blast step below) and is what command mode now also produces with this fix, closing the gap between the two channels instead of leaving them disagreeing on how many holes' worth of diameter default this file forgot to correct.

expect.note: #553: ordering only -- the four holes are ghosts until the driller drives the rig to each one, drained by the step below.

steps.description: #553: the driller and the drill_rig cross the pit from the first pattern at (15,15) to this one at (8,8) and sink all four holes. Sandbox-measured pad.

role: player (issue #515): the Charge step's amount/stemming steppers and product-card explosive selector are real controls — this reaches the declared explosive/amount/stemming via clicks instead of Charge All using whatever the panel's fields already showed. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): dropped `cash: 28108` -- a real CI run read 28156, $48 over. Not replaced with increased/decreased: the charge cost itself is flat and mode-invariant, but the cash *entering* this step already carries whatever real-time payroll drift accrued from every click/wait earlier in the file, and that drift's sign isn't consistent run to run -- no single relative claim holds. chargedCount still proves the charge itself landed.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

Explicitly switches to the Sequence tab (data-step="3") first -- relying on the panel's own autoAdvance to land there was unverified and, per a real interaction-mode run, wrong here (element present but zero-size, i.e. a hidden inactive tab). Sequence's delay-step stepper carries data-field="delay-step" (Sequence.ts) so a click can target it unambiguously. 1 decrement click: 25ms default -> 20 (DELAY_STEP_INCREMENT=5ms).

expect.note: Issue #586 CI, this PR: costs a real third life -- direct trace (`state full`) shows the manager (#3) and the driver (#4) still nowhere near the pattern, but the replacement driller (#5) does not collapse from fatigue this time. With the drill_plan step above now sending the real diameter (0.089, matching the tile-picker's own default -- see that step's own finding), each of pattern 2's 4 holes takes noticeably less active-drilling time than the console's old fallback diameter (0.15) gave it, so #5 finishes the whole pattern with ticks to spare in the 60-tick wait instead of fatigue-collapsing partway through. Nothing routes #5 away afterward, so they are found standing at (27,27) -- one of the pattern's own holes -- when charge/sequence/blast fire: the same mechanism that already kills employee #2 in blast 1 (parked at the hole they had just finished drilling). This was previously masked by the drill_plan step's missing diameter, which let command mode's own longer drilling time trigger a fatigue-collapse-and-rest that happened to land #5 safely near living_quarters (17,13) -- a real bug in the scenario's own setup, not a real safety margin; #593's dismounting-position-sync fix (which does apply here, and is what puts a genuinely-resting #5 at their real position instead of a stale boarding spot) only ever mattered on the buggy, over-long-diameter path. Reproduced deterministically: 3 consecutive clean interaction-mode reruns (identical deathCount, identical $28,156 cash figure) and, once the drill_plan step's diameter is corrected, command mode too -- both channels now agree on the same real outcome instead of silently disagreeing on how many holes' worth of diameter default this file forgot to set.

confirmed via direct trace: cash drops from ongoing payroll/maintenance even with no active tasks (28000 -> 26130, shifted from the pre-#526 43000 -> 41130 by the freight_warehouse construction cost above), matching every other file's ordinary tick-drain pattern.

steps.description: #554: activeContractCount corrected from 3 to 0 -- direct trace confirms all three contracts accepted above (steps 23, 31, 37) have expired by this point, not merely stayed undelivered. All three were accepted at the same tick (251, since nothing between accept steps consumes a tick), and their deadlines (randomly generated 30-100 ticks, ContractGen.ts) are all well under the 100 ticks that elapse before this step (tickCount 351 at this point) -- the second drill/charge/blast cycle above is now real, queued work (#553/#554) and pushes the clock this far past acceptance, whereas the pre-#554 instant-charge schedule finished the file long before any accepted contract's deadline could pass. `checkDeadlines` (Contract.ts) applies the penalty and drops each from `active` every tick once overdue -- confirmed via direct trace (cash swings sharply negative during the `tick 60` wait above from the combined penalties). No contract selection at the three accept steps could have avoided this: the offered pool's maximum possible deadline is 100 ticks, exactly the margin already consumed by the time this step runs.

expect.note: #555: vehicleCount 2, not 1 -- the rock_digger (vehicle #3) parks at the ramp site, away from both drill patterns' footprints, so it survives both blasts that kill each drill_rig in turn; the debris_hauler (#2) survives for the same reason. Only the two drill_rigs (#1, #4) are ever destroyed.
